claims.text: A business plan to be handed to whoever wants to build it: a service that helps companies manage the cost of agentic AI by observing what is already happening in their estate.
claims.quote: help companies manage the cost of agentic AI, by observing what is already happening

claims.text: It is a business rather than a consulting engagement because the inputs exist in every company with agents in production, nobody reads them together, and the two outputs, a shorter bill and a map of what to build, are things companies pay for.
claims.quote: The reason I think it is a business, and not a consulting engagement

claims.text: Cost is an engineering problem: an unexplained agent bill is an estate that shipped from the explorer side without the villager's discipline, a class of defect with a cause, a fix and a test, not a discount to negotiate.
claims.quote: not a thing you fix by negotiating a discount, but a class of defect with a cause, a fix and a test

claims.text: Agents almost always come from a session: a prompt that worked, wrapped in a workflow, sent to production because it worked, which is the explorer side of the map, the right place to build and the wrong place to run at scale.
claims.quote: That is the explorer side of the map, genesis and custom-built, and it is the right place to build something new.

claims.text: What agents run on is commodity billed by use: the invoice exact, the logs complete, the traces written whether asked or not, nobody reading them together, and the owner of cost, the node that should connect bill to agents, missing.
claims.quote: the one node on the map that should connect the bill to the agents, an owner of cost, is missing

claims.text: An agent that retries in a loop is a bug, a workflow that sends its whole context on every call is a bug, and a key with no ceiling is a missing control; the service exists to make them visible.
claims.quote: An agent that retries in a loop is a bug.

claims.text: The service installs nothing: the customer drops invoices by key and day, logs and traces, prompts, workflow files and schedules into a vault they own, sealed to the service's key.
claims.quote: No agent is installed and nothing in the customer's environment is changed.

claims.text: The footprint of every agent, read from the logs, calls, tokens, tools, retries, loops, hours and data touched, is the after-the-fact twin of a mandate and the first thing the money attaches to.
claims.quote: here it is the first thing the money attaches to

claims.text: The twin of the estate is a graph of agents, models, keys, tools, data, owners and schedules with a cost on every edge, which can be queried, compared with the invoice and followed; the connector twin is one component of it.
claims.quote: a graph of agents, models, keys, tools, data, owners and schedules, with a cost on every edge

claims.text: The policy each agent was in fact running under is written as an Agent Behaviour Policy from the footprint, with the enforcement column filled honestly so the rows that rest on being told are visible, where cost and risk both sit.
claims.quote: because that is where both the cost and the risk are

claims.text: The gaps, no log, no owner, no policy, no cap, go on the map as findings, not as missing data.
claims.quote: These go on the map as findings, not as missing data.

claims.text: Two lists in order: the cost list first, loops disguised as retries, whole context per call, big models where small ones answer, unread schedules, keys with no ceiling, because it pays for the engagement; then the engineering list, the reason to have it.
claims.quote: The cost list first, because it pays for the engagement

claims.text: Sending the whole context on every call when a graph would send a slice is a cost The agent is the reader measured at ninety per cent less.
claims.quote: measured at ninety per cent less

value.unit: percent less context when a graph sends a slice

claims.text: A cost review is bought once and resented, a map of what to build is returned to, so the service sells cost reduction and delivers engineering opportunity, and the business model follows the second.
claims.quote: So the service sells cost reduction, and delivers engineering opportunity, and the business model follows the second.

claims.text: A company that cannot produce a log for an agent has an agent nobody is watching; not being able to do the analysis is the first result of the analysis, and the one most companies need first.
claims.quote: Not being able to do the analysis is the first result of the analysis

claims.text: Capture: the customer's logs go into a vault once, encrypted in their browser or on their machine, in a vault they own and can revoke; the service holds a read key and nothing else.
claims.quote: The service holds a read key to that vault and nothing else.

claims.text: Transform: every step from invoice to finding is a commit, so a finding can be followed back to the lines it rests on, the same provenance rule the newsroom runs on.
claims.quote: Every step from invoice to finding is a commit

claims.text: Move: anonymised extracts leave as sealed envelopes to a benchmark vault, seen by the customer before they go, and over time that vault lets the service say what companies like yours spend, which is the second business.
claims.quote: Over time that vault is the thing that lets the service say

claims.text: Four price levels on the RiskMandate pattern: a Kit at £50, Your cost vault at £250, Standard at £3,000 with a board summary within ten working days, Tailored from £9,000, and a share-of-savings option.
claims.quote: a one-page board summary, within ten working days

value.unit: GBP for a Standard estate read, an assumption

claims.text: About eight Standard and two Tailored a month cover a two-founder burn, on the same arithmetic as Company X-Ray; every number is a labelled assumption.
claims.quote: About eight Standard and two Tailored a month cover a two-founder burn

value.unit: Standard reads a month, with two Tailored, to cover a two-founder burn

claims.text: What exists: the footprint method, the behaviour policy format with its enforcement column, the connector twin design, the vault tooling, the sealed envelopes, and the Company X-Ray pattern of reading a company's documents in a vault.
claims.quote: the Company X-Ray pattern of reading a company's own documents in a vault and returning findings in five days

claims.text: What does not exist: the catalogue of cost analyses, the twin schema for an agent estate, the log parsers for common platforms, the benchmark vault, and a single customer; a few weeks of work.
claims.quote: That is the work, and it is a few weeks of it, which is why I am writing the plan rather than keeping it.

claims.text: No customer has been read; the method is assembled from pieces that run elsewhere, and the two lists are what the owner expects to find, not what has been found.
claims.quote: No customer has been read.

claims.text: The prices are assumptions, labelled as such on the pattern of the other plans, to be tested against the first three customers.
claims.quote: The prices are assumptions. Labelled as such, on the pattern of the other plans here

claims.text: The map is a sketch: Wardley maps are arguments, not measurements, and this one says where the owner thinks the problem sits and why.
claims.quote: Wardley maps are arguments, not measurements

claims.text: Share of savings is hard to measure honestly: it needs a baseline from the invoices and an agreed way to attribute a reduction, which the plan should say before anyone signs.
claims.quote: Share of savings is hard to measure honestly.

claims.text: The plan comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026 after a conversation with an unnamed possible collaborator, written by the site's agent; the Wardley maps and the plan figure were drawn for the article.
claims.quote: after a conversation with someone I may collaborate with; they are not named

the vaults that carry the data in, the transformations as commits, and the extracts out
the site's own explorer-to-villager move, and the provenance rule the transformations copy
the owner, whose plan and editorial responsibility this is
